title: An operator and an autoscaler can read that encoding is falling behind, and why
description: docs/running.md calls jellyscale_transcode_queue_cores the signal to scale workers on, but a play with no free cores is refused, not queued, and a re-encode running under real time is not queued either, so on the dogfood's stalled plays (2026-11-20) that signal read nothing. This task adds one cluster-wide number for demand beyond what the workers hold, with its reason, pulled forward from JS-021 criterion 5. PRODUCT.md: the cluster can grow and shrink with demand by itself; a heavy film uses the whole cluster's processors.
acceptanceCriteria: Observed first with real processes and recorded: what jellyscale_transcode_queue_cores reads while (a) a watched re-encode runs under real time with no helper possible and (b) a play is refused for lack of free cores. If it reads 0 in both, docs/running.md no longer calls it the signal to scale on. JS-162 read 0 at one snapshot of each stalling run (case a, once per run); case b is still unobserved.

A gauge on /metrics gives, in cores and for the whole cluster, the demand the workers do not hold, by reason: jobs queued; helpers wanted by a watched job under 1.2 times real time and not started for lack of room; plays refused for lack of free cores within a stated recent window, and, as its own reason, plays refused because the cores are held by a helper another viewer's film needs (JS-161 criterion 11). Every worker reports the same number, as queue_cores does Whichever replica refuses, a play refused for a held film is logged and counted with the held-film reason, never as cores short or busy (JS-161 minor).

Each reason is above zero within 15 seconds of its condition starting and back to zero within a stated time of its ending, so an autoscaler both grows and shrinks on it; checked with two real workers for each reason

A second gauge gives, for the whole cluster and in reference cores, the dearest job a new viewer would be admitted for now, by JS-161's rule (one worker or shared). Cores held by a helper of a watched job its own worker does not hold at 1.2 times real time alone are not free; cores held by any other helper are (JS-161 criterion 11). It falls within 15 seconds of a play starting and rises within a stated time of its ending, checked with two real workers, a viewer's job and a helper. An operator or an autoscaler keeps it above the dearest job they want to start without a wait, so no viewer has to be refused or stall to trigger growth.
Not counted as demand: a job no viewer watches, a paused job, a copy reading at its own rate, and helpers when transcodeHelpers is off; docs/running.md says which slowness more workers cannot fix
The only label is the reason: never a job, film, account or device

docs/running.md's metric table and docs/transcoding.md describe both gauges with an example alert and an example scaling query; BL-005's missing reason is readable here. the example scaling query is on the room gauge, the example alert on the demand gauge; docs/running.md no longer calls `jellyscale_transcode_queue_cores` the signal to scale on, and says why.
notes: ux: true (operators). If JS-161 changes what a refusal for cores means, this counts JS-161's.
